items.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: That’s right. He’s a very dear friend of mine too, Eddie.

ctx.x: I talked with Eddie Bert, who was often the only white player in black bands.
That’s right. He’s a very dear friend of mine too, Eddie.
Yeah. He’s a wonderful guy. I interviewed him, and he said that it was interesting, because to him, “We were all just musicians.”

items.title: Eddie Bert interviewed by Monk Rowe, Danbury, Connecticut, November 20, 2001
items.q: Because when I went to Manhattan School of Music, Max Roach was there, John Lewis was there, Joe Wilder was there

ctx.x: I never heard that particular term before, “he’s a roadie.”

Yeah well in other words you get a name that you’re always on the road, which I was, but I couldn’t do anything about it. Even though I was from New York, I couldn’t get into that core. But eventually I did by going to school. Because when I went to Manhattan School of Music, Max Roach was there, John Lewis was there, Joe Wilder was there, and there was all, it was like a jazz school almost.
But you weren’t taking jazz courses, right?
